candidates.label: The JJ store's entries need a four-way disposition, version-bound, and pointers must be rewritten on restore
candidates.assertion: The closure record classifies every captured JJ store entry as shared_content (portable), host_local_pathmap (captured but non-authoritative, requiring rebind before use), pointer (captured with both raw bytes and resolved target), or ephemeral_lock (captured for forensics only, never restored as active state); an entry matching none is `unclassified` and forces closure_state: partial. The classification BINDS the exact discovered JJ repo-format version it was audited against, so a store at a different version degrades to unclassified rather than assuming parity. Restore rebinds path maps, drops locks, rewrites pointers to stay inside the isolated boundary, and verification fails closed if any pointer or path map still resolves outside it.

This is the specific structural consequence: layout_profile has NO value for 'JJ repo backed by an external Git repository at an absolute path', such a repo presents as non_colocated while its object store lives outside everything the capture walked, and git_common_directory_ref is permitted to be null for non_colocated - so complete validates over an absent store. The isolation half is worse: a restored git_target still resolving to the original machine path means the 'isolated' copy opens the ORIGINAL Git store.

candidates.label: A capture blocked for a non-dependency reason is UNREPRESENTABLE in both closure schemas
candidates.assertion: The state 'the capture barrier was lost, but no dependency is missing' cannot be recorded at any completeness value. capture_completeness = complete REQUIRES barrier_outcome = held_during_capture and gc_fence_outcome = held_during_capture; capture_completeness in {partial, blocked} REQUIRES missing_dependency_refs minItems 1; additionalProperties is false and the required list contains no blocked-reason field of any kind. So {barrier_outcome: lost_during_capture, missing_dependency_refs: []} is forbidden at complete by the barrier rule and at partial and blocked by the minItems rule. The same trap applies to not_acquired and to both non-held values of gc_fence_outcome, and BackupJujutsuClosureRecord reproduces the second half.

candidates.label: FileSafe's safe-point profile is defined entirely in Git terms and has no Jujutsu profile
candidates.assertion: Three owner documents require FileSafe to work for Jujutsu, and the FileSafe owner document never mentions Jujutsu at all. The safe-point worktree manifest REQUIRES repo_id, worktree_id, canonical worktree-root identity, branch name, exact HEAD OID and Git index entries and stages, plus Git mode or submodule gitlink OID - none of which exists in a non-colocated JJ workspace, which has no Git index, no Git HEAD and no .git at the worktree root, while mutations still require a FileSafe decision. Membership of the .jj store is left to Git ignore evaluation the Plans never specify for a JJ workspace, and FileSafe's exact-replace restore would rewind the Jujutsu operation store as ordinary bytes - the outcome :190 forbids.

candidates.label: A 32nd canonical command, cmd.jujutsu.bookmark.forget
candidates.assertion: Add cmd.jujutsu.bookmark.forget so a user whose intent is 'stop tracking this locally, leave the remote alone' has a covered route. At v0.44.0 forget is the ONLY native way to drop a local bookmark without queueing a remote deletion, and native delete's own help text points users at it. Both jobs raise it independently and both recommend NOT exposing --include-remotes in a first cut, because the next fetch recreates the remote bookmark if it still exists upstream - an action that visibly undoes itself.

candidates.label: An edge kind for elided ancestry, and page arithmetic that is checkable
candidates.assertion: Add indirect_ancestor to the closed edges[].kind enum plus an optional elided_count, and state in SCS-017 that an edge spanning omitted revisions renders as indirect and never as a direct parent. A 200-node page of a filtered history - and Jujutsu's DEFAULT log revset is filtered - will routinely contain two visible nodes whose real relationship is 'ancestor, with hidden commits between', so rendering kind: parent asserts something false and omitting the edge hides the relationship.

observations.label: THE RESULT: doubling admissions bought FIVE union findings and cost two
observations.detail: A24 scored 43/110 against claude-hicap's 45 - a net of MINUS TWO - while comparing 26 leads to hicap's 14 and spending $162.15 against $82.52. The comparison is exact rather than approximate: hicap's fourteen compared leads are a STRICT SUBSET of A24's twenty-six, and the split falls on a job boundary. A24's first six compare jobs carry precisely hicap's fourteen leads and earned 38; its last four carry twelve leads hicap never reached and earned 5 findings the first six had not already produced (F005, F025, F027, F057, F086). Credits per compared lead fall from 2.71 on the first fourteen to 0.42 on the next twelve - a 6.5x collapse.
observations.adjudicator_note: Recorded as the arm's result and the answer to the admission-budget question.

observations.label: The variance floor is confirmed a second time, independently
observations.detail: On lead sets that were IDENTICAL, with the same model at the same effort and no limit reached by either run, A24 earned 38 where claude-hicap earned 45 - a seven-finding difference from run-to-run variance alone. T80 measured eight on four jobs; A24 measures seven on six. Two independent estimates, 7 and 8, on the same case and the same model. That is now the best-supported number in the campaign, and it means EVERY arm-to-arm difference in continuation 5 smaller than about eight findings is indistinguishable from noise: A24 versus hicap (-2), A24 versus Arm B (+4), Arm B versus hicap (-6) are all inside it. Only Arm P (-13), T80 (-19) and A24 versus T80 (+17) are outside.
observations.adjudicator_note: Recorded, and it is the single most important qualifier on every table in this bundle.

observations.label: The three stopped jobs are the sentinel, not money, and the label says otherwise
observations.detail: All three carry runtime_status budget_truncated and bound_by budget. The journal shows the arm had committed $176.46 of a $300 cap when the sentinel pinned a headroom-sized hold of $145.19 on a typed five-hour allowed_warning at utilization 0.90, taking committed-with-hold to $321.66 and denying the next request on three live jobs with reason captured_plus_live_cap. This is the same adapter-labelling caveat I recorded for deepseek41 in continuation 4 and it must be read from the journal, not the status. The hold also behaved exactly as designed: it fired after all 24 admissions were spent so it cost no admissions, live jobs settled to their own terminals rather than being cancelled, and all 24 jobs reconciled with $0.00 unresolved - the cleanest accounting of any arm in either continuation.

observations.label: A high-quality job can produce zero marginal union credit
observations.detail: J0031-compare is the campaign's sharpest statement that $defs/command_result carries NO condition on `cancelled` beyond 'has an error payload', so a cancelled cmd.jujutsu.git.push may report effect_state: none with a null after_revision and validate - and it proves the corpus's one cancelled fixture is clone, the single operation where absence of effect is provable because the destination is new. Every union finding it reaches (F007, F074, F081) had already been earned from the first fourteen leads. Three fresh leads, real new work, zero marginal credit against a fixed union. This is what the 0.42-per-lead figure is made of, and it is a property of measuring against a FIXED union as much as of the leads.

observations.label: A24 bounds the external-editor blast radius that three earlier arms left unbounded
observations.detail: J0020 verified the whole matcher chain first-hand at its own pinned commit and resolved what it had listed as an open uncertainty: the effective snapshot matcher is IntersectionMatcher(sparse_matcher, UnionMatcher(fsmonitor_matcher, force_tracking_matcher)); a None fsmonitor matcher falls through to EverythingMatcher; and diff_working_copies passes force_tracking_matcher: &NothingMatcher - so the union is EverythingMatcher and the intersection is EXACTLY the sparse set. A file the editor creates at a path outside changed_files is NOT snapshotted; a file it writes at a changed path is picked up with no prompt because start_tracking_matcher is EverythingMatcher. I re-verified both source sites against the arm's own checkout. The arm's conclusion is the honest one: 'the blast radius should not be described as unbounded'. That is a correction to the campaign's own earlier framing, made by an arm against itself.
observations.adjudicator_note: Recorded as the arm's best single piece of verification work.

observations.label: A24 adds nothing to the campaign union
observations.detail: Every one of A24's 43 credits was already reached by an earlier arm. The ten-arm union stays at 62 of 110 (56.36%) and findings reached by no arm stay at 48. Three continuation-5 arms in a row - P, T80 and A24 - have now added zero; only Arm B extended the union, by three. Against a fixed union built from premium and hybrid output, more of the same model on more of the same leads does not reach further.
